question: to the Commission Michael McNamara (Renew) Subject:

In its proposal revising the Cybersecurity Act1, the Commission proposes phasing out ICT components from high-risk suppliers for key ICT assets of mobile, fixed and satellite electronic communications networks. The Commission’s impact assessment2 recognises that mobile network operators would incur direct and indirect substitution and transaction costs to replace relevant 5G equipment from high-risk suppliers with comparable alternatives throughout the EU. The impact assessment estimates a one-off cost of EUR 3.4 billion to EUR 4.3 billion, or EUR 6.50 to EUR 8.30 per mobile subscriber if the cost is fully passed on to consumers. While strengthening resilience in the sector is an important priority, industry estimates that the actual cost of this provision would be substantially higher (EUR 730 million in Ireland alone)3. The provision could therefore have an unintended negative impact on resilience. 1.
What sources and methodologies were used and what consultations were held by the Commission for its impact assessment to arrive at these figures?
How does the Commission explain the substantial disparity between its own estimates and industry’s estimates?
In the light of these proposals, what steps is the Commission taking to ensure that industry can advance connectivity targets, provide quality services for consumers and strengthen resilience?

Commission proposal of 20 January 2026 for a regulation of the European Parliament and of the Council on the European Union Agency for Cybersecurity (ENISA), the European cybersecurity certification framework, and ICT supply chain security and repealing Regulation (EU) 2019/881 (The Cybersecurity Act 2) (COM(2026)0011). 2 https://ec.europa.eu/newsroom/dae/redirection/document/123748. 3 https://www.ibec.ie/connect-and-learn/media/2026/04/15/eu-cybersecurity-act-review-presentsconcerns-for-irish-business-new-ibec-report. 1
